key_insight: Model annotator behavior and systematically decide to trust, ignore, or flip each preference signal—producing reward models and policies that remain accurate even when some annotators are noisy or adversarial.
problem_solved: Preference-based RL (PBRL) degrades when feedback comes from heterogeneous annotators (accurate, noisy, or adversarial). The paper solves robustly learning rewards and policies from multi-expert pairwise comparisons without assuming all feedback is honest.
method: Infer per-expert reliability and systematic bias from multi-expert pairwise comparisons (probabilistic annotator model).
Triage each feedback instance into three actions—trust, discard, or flip—based on inferred reliability and consistency with the emerging reward signal.
Integrate the triage-adjusted preferences into reward-model training and downstream RL (robust loss / iterative EM-style refinement) to produce stable policies under adversarial noise.
impact: Enables practitioners to train RL agents from crowdsourced or mixed-quality human feedback with far less manual curation and higher tolerance to adversarial annotators, improving real-world deployment and scaling of preference-based learning.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: multi-expert preference inputs → annotator reliability inference → triage (Trust / Don’t Trust / Flip) → reward model → RL policy.
Bar chart: policy performance vs. fraction of adversarial annotators comparing baseline PBRL, filtering approaches, and the proposed method.
Heatmap: inferred annotator reliability / bias across experts (clear adversarial cluster visible).
Icon set: simple icons for 'trust', 'trash/ignore', and 'flip/invert' to communicate the triage rule succinctly.
paper_title: Trust, Don't Trust, or Flip: Robust Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Expert Feedback
paper_authors: Seyed Amir Hosseini, Maryam Abdolali, Amirhosein Tavakkoli, Fardin Ayar, Ehsan Javanmardi
